fact: We Are Tech Africa reports that the government presented DIGI-CoR, a CFA 92 billion (US$163 million) programme over three years, to technical and financial partners in Yaoundé on 2 June 2026; it is to deploy digital infrastructure, improve connectivity, equip decentralised local authorities with IT and energy systems and set up interoperable platforms.

We Are Tech Africa states that DIGI-CoR is the government's own programme for the decentralised local authorities, presented by it to partners on 2 June 2026, with local authorities to rely on shared resources for hosting, cybersecurity and service management.

We Are Tech Africa states that on 2 June 2026 Cameroon was still seeking financing for DIGI-CoR's CFA 92 billion from technical and financial partners; no domestic budget line and no committed funder is named.

On 2 June 2026 the government presented DIGI-CoR, a CFA 92 billion programme that includes improving the connectivity of decentralised local authorities, to funders in Yaoundé; the programme was unfunded and nothing was reported as deployed.

fact: Centrifuge Hebdo, reporting the presentation of the first phase of the communes' digitalisation programme in Yaoundé on 11 September 2025, lists the weakness of ICT infrastructure and of connectivity at commune level among the constraints still threatening it; no count of communes connected is given, against 360 communes and 14 urban communities.

The town halls of Mayo-Oulo and Bibemi, in the North region, were each fitted with at least one Wi-Fi access point joined by a long-distance Wi-Fi link to the postal digital access point at Mayo-Oulo, which has fibre, and to the Bibemi community telecentre, under a pilot agreed between the telecommunications ministry and GIZ's PRADEC programme after studies in 2018, as APC's policy brief states; the brief gives no date for the installation, so the fact is dated to its publication in 2023, and it does not say who pays for the link.

fact: The pilot networks at Mayo-Oulo and Bibemi give the connected sites, the two town halls among them, internet access and offline access to the GOON platform of local content, as APC's brief of 2023 states; it names no use by the town halls' staff and no national system worked in. system: réseaux maillés Wi-Fi autour des télécentres (PRADEC)

fact: Two communes' town halls, Mayo-Oulo and Bibemi, are named as sites connected by the pilot networks, among 4 sites at Mayo-Oulo and the sites listed at Bibemi, on APC's brief of 2023; no total of communes connected is given. Dated to publication.

fact: The equipment of the pilot networks that reach the two town halls was acquired by GIZ's PRADEC programme, the only funder the brief of 2023 names for them; the brief adds that telecommunications is not a power transferred to local authorities, so their own funds cannot be used for such networks.
